missionPremise: DO NOT MAKE THE STORE THE PREDICATE (OPS-24 Law 1; A-183 in the dispatch preamble): the customer predicate is `scripts/surface-probe.mjs` driven across real fixtures, not a stage's private check and not a store-reading instrument, because the factory-store and atoms-store instruments were green through the whole 2026-09-15 map incident. This lane is the CUSTOMER LEG of the Phase 0 exit (scope rev 4 section 5, exit condition 2): grade what a customer reaches - the map payload, the MCP and the PDF - over the delivered bucket fixture list, so a county's completion is something observable rather than a ledger count. Two standing rulings bound what may be graded CORRECT: ENVELOPE DRAWN, FIGURE REFUSED (operator 2026-09-11, `_decisions/2026-09-11_ruling_b_reversed_polygon_only.md`) - the modelled envelope may draw wherever a district and a setback table exist, but buildable area and percent stay refused until a verdict-backed envelope atom exists (A-180), which the MCP payload and the PDF do not enforce today (P-249, P-261) - and MOST-CURRENT SOURCE WINS with the P-178 vintage rule (operator 2026-09-11), which makes an undated setback citation a conflict row rather than a silent pick. The dispatch's two REQUIRED CASES are the reason the instrument must compare surfaces against EACH OTHER: a false cross-surface reason is invisible to any surface graded against itself.

LESSON: A defect indicator can be STRUCTURALLY BLIND to the population it names and still print as measured. XD-7 was literally 'Williamson: no composed address' and returned UNMEASURED whenever the payload carried no situs - which is the Williamson shape - so the ledger read CLOSED with the condition in front of it, on every run, silently. The test that catches it is cheap and belongs in every defect grader: assert the grader FIRES on the shape its own defect name describes, using a payload read live from that population.

A grader's BASIS STRING is part of the instrument, because the close quotes it. XD-7's fixed basis said 'no address of any kind: no situs, no composed address and no coordinate' - false for the Bastrop parcels, which carry a record point and drew 6 vertices from it. Assert basis WORDING in both directions (present vs absent) when the basis makes a claim about which fields are missing.

README the payload's absence shapes before writing any extractor on them. A panel field can be a plain null, or an inline absence OBJECT with `{status, verdict, authority, scopeSearched}` naming the authority and the search scope. Any normaliser that keeps only truthy strings collapses the second into the first and destroys the difference between 'we looked and it is not there' and 'we have nothing' - which AGENT_CONTRACT section 5 exists to protect.

When two counts of the same phenomenon differ, print BOTH with their rules rather than reconciling them into one: legsTripping (7) vs kindCounts (10) look like a bug and are not, because one counts legs and the other counts kind-instances of two kinds. A reader who cannot see both numbers has to trust the author; a reader who can see both can check the arithmetic.

A per-bucket VERDICT and a defect LEDGER answer different questions and a close that emits only one of them is misleading: the 12-parcel XD-7 population sits inside 28 buckets whose verdict is UNMEASURED, and 17 buckets FAIL on the map and draw surfaces alone. Emitting both, with their own counting rules, is what lets a reader see both truths at once.
